source_review.notes: Checked the formal OMG SysML v1-to-v2 Transformation, SysML 2.0 Language, KerML 1.0 and Systems Modeling API and Services 1.0 publications; current OMG QVT 1.3 and MOF Model to Text 1.0 specification pages and PDFs; and current NASA Software Engineering and Assurance Handbook Version D SWE-146 and SWE-206 guidance. All ten final URLs returned HTTP 200. Claims distinguish normative language/transformation standards, general transformation concepts and project-specific auto-generated-code assurance.

evidence: Reviewed the compilation judgment over source model/metamodel, rules, libraries, environment, target, trace and diagnostics.
Reviewed precondition, target conformance, postcondition, target-test and critical-diagnostic acceptance conjunction.
Reviewed property-specific semantic preservation through explicit abstraction mapping alpha rather than unqualified equivalence.
Reviewed run record, many-to-many trace relation, disposition completeness and full-versus-incremental regeneration equivalence.
Reviewed executable-source/target commuting relation and bounded its finite testing interpretation.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation treats semantic preservation as named obligations under assumptions; it does not claim a universal transformation theorem.

evidence: Executed state-transform-codegen-fixture under python3 with exact output recorded in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-058/report.json.
Confirmed three declared states, four transitions, eleven generated text lines and four source-to-line trace entries.
Confirmed reversed source enumeration regenerates byte-identical output after stable sorting.
Confirmed required generated structures are present, every source/target state resolves and all three states are reachable from IDLE.
Confirmed the transformed target table passes all four declared transition cases.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture intentionally does not parse, compile or execute emitted code; its structural string checks and target-table cases are synthetic subset evidence only.

evidence: Confirmed target acceptance requires source preconditions, target conformance, cross-model postconditions, target tests and absence of critical diagnostics.
Confirmed unsupported source properties require explicit loss or unknown disposition rather than vacuous preservation.
Confirmed trace completeness allows mapped, approved omission, externalization or unresolved status and does not treat unresolved as success.
Confirmed incremental correctness compares the incrementally updated target to a clean full transformation after the same source change.
Confirmed commuting execution tests are bounded by input domain and require explicit source/target semantics and abstraction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No general equivalence is inferred from compilation, trace existence, visual similarity or finite behavior cases.

evidence: Challenged invalid/partial sources, unsupported constructs, information loss, overlapping rule dispatch, defaults, recursion and nondeterministic traversal.
Reviewed stable identity under rename/move, deletes/orphans, one-to-many/many-to-one trace, stale incremental dependencies and clean rebuilds.
Reviewed round-trip authority, protected-region loss, manual forks, generated-versus-handwritten separation and migration-versus-derivation.
Reviewed locale/time/encoding/random ID churn, partial-output promotion, formatter noise, runtime/library drift and long-term reproducibility.
Reviewed reserved identifiers, Unicode, string/path/config injection, secret emission, vulnerable dependencies and platform adapters.
Reviewed compiler/static analysis limits, source-reference differential cases, target numeric/timing/concurrency/resource/fault behavior and system validation.
Reviewed tool qualification scope, generator common-mode defects, upgrades, affected-output impact and deployed discrepancy feedback.
Reviewed all ten worked examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limits and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Consequential generation still requires applicable metamodel/transformation, compiler, target-language, runtime/platform, security, safety, numerical, integration, verification, validation, qualification and technical-authority review.

evidence: Traced source/target metamodels, libraries/profiles, transformation/templates/generator, platform/runtime and environment versions throughout.
Confirmed source validation, semantic mapping, loss disposition, target conformance and target behavior remain separate gates.
Confirmed every consequential source and target has trace/disposition and one declared authority.
Confirmed deterministic generation, regeneration, full-versus-incremental comparison and atomic promotion retain explicit obligations.
Confirmed generated code is held to product standards appropriate to intended use and generator evidence does not replace target/system evidence.
Confirmed changes anywhere in the source-to-runtime chain trigger impact analysis and proportionate replay.
invariant_checking.notes: Trace and reproducibility support auditability but never substitute for semantic or product correctness.

proof_review.notes: The chapter presents preservation obligations and commuting relations but no theorem proof.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Reviewed generated, deterministic, conformant, semantically preserved, equivalent, qualified, verified, validated, safe and reproducible language for scope.
The executable evidence is labeled synthetic_subset_only and explicitly does not parse, compile or execute the emitted code.
Compilation and trace existence are repeatedly denied status as semantic equivalence or system acceptance.
NASA auto-generation guidance is used for configuration/V&V obligations without claiming the handbook qualifies any project tool.
Vendor/tool qualification evidence is bounded by version, configuration, platform, feature subset and intended use.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No external review, qualified generator, product compliance, safety assurance or real-system validation is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked model-to-model/text, endogenous/exogenous, horizontal/vertical, declarative/imperative, rule, trace, preservation/refinement, information loss, code generation, determinism, round trip, incremental transformation, protected region, qualification, derivation and migration. These concepts remain distinct throughout.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked transformation contracts, source preconditions, semantic mappings, deterministic dispatch, identity/traces/loss, incremental and round-trip behavior, compiler pipelines, generated/manual separation, escaping, runtime dependencies, fixture strategies, semantic/target tests, tool qualification, reproducible builds, causal diffs, atomic failure and deployment monitoring. Cases cover exports, units, rule order, renames, deletes, manual patches, injection, golden outputs, runtime mismatch and upgrades.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from transformation taxonomy and contracts through mapping/trace mechanics, code-generation assurance and lifecycle governance. Ten examples isolate recurring defects; five complete solutions require design of a safety-relevant pipeline, repair of a weak generator, incremental correctness, v1-to-v2 migration acceptance and high-churn generator-upgrade evaluation.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external OMG/QVT/MOFM2T/SysML expert, compiler or generator expert, tool-vendor, target-platform/runtime, cybersecurity, software assurance, safety, numerical, integration, independent V&V, qualification/accreditation, technical-authority or decision-authority review is claimed.
